about: pqam/0.1 conformance cases against ap2-evidence-pack 1.10.0 (SPEC_AP2_EVIDENCE.md, 2026-11-22) and the AER-1 anchor outcomes. Revision 2: corrected from a 1.10.0 run on AP2 #338.

rows.pack_today: sealed_content verified; holder_binding verified (KB-JWT)
rows.pack_with_issuance_member: same, plus the issuance signature verified at the mandate

rows.pack_today: sealed_content verified; holder_binding verified

rows.name: edited limit after signing
rows.pack_today: sealed_content contradicted (artifact_invalid: issuer signature)

rows.name: PQ signature removed (classical half only)
rows.pack_today: no issuer-PQ member exists, so the ES256 mandate alone reads sealed_content verified

rows.name: Q-Day forgery: real classical signature + attacker's ML-DSA under the issuer's kid
rows.pack_today: the forged ES256 mandate verifies: sealed_content verified. A fresh pack and a fresh anchor verify too. This is the gap.
rows.pack_with_issuance_member: contradicted at the mandate: the PQ half fails

rows.name: Q-Day forgery with the attacker's own kid
rows.pack_today: as above: verified
rows.pack_with_issuance_member: contradicted (a signer outside the signed key list)

rows.name: unknown algorithm in the signature list
rows.pack_today: the nearest rule is the producer block's: an unknown sig_alg is a GAP (not_evaluated), and the block is never ok
rows.pack_with_issuance_member: pqam refuses an unknown algorithm outright (UnknownAlgorithm). Neither accepts it, but the words differ: not_evaluated vs. a failure

rows.name: not accepted by the agent
rows.pack_today: holder_binding not_evaluated (not_present): no KB-JWT. That is a failure only if the relying party requires holder binding
rows.pack_with_issuance_member: pqam: NotAccepted is a verification failure. Acceptance is required, not a relying-party option

rows.name: accepted by a key that is not the agent's
rows.pack_today: holder_binding contradicted (kb_signature_invalid)

rows.name: issuer signature made under the accept tag
rows.pack_today: a mandate with typ kb+jwt reads valid: true. typ is checked on the KB-JWT (§6 step 2, §9.2) and on delegation-chain hops after the first (§2.1), not on a mandate outside a chain
rows.pack_with_issuance_member: contradicted at the mandate: pqam's type tag is inside the signed bytes
rows.run: run 1.10.0: corrected from the first reading

rows.pack_with_issuance_member: verified. Whether it is acceptable is policy: see the admission rows

rows.name: issuer with ML-DSA-44 only (verifies; admission decides)
rows.pack_today: no ML-DSA-44 in the pack's algorithm set
rows.pack_with_issuance_member: verified (pq_level 2). Admission refuses it under min_pq_level 3

rows.name: amount as a JSON number
rows.pack_today: depends on where the number sits. Inside the mandate an integer amount is admitted and reads valid: true, and a fraction reads sealed_content contradicted (artifact_invalid, sd_number_fraction). admission refused / malformed applies only to a fraction in the pack file itself
rows.run: run 1.10.0: corrected from the first reading

rows.pack_with_issuance_member: pqam: Malformed (the mandate's own fields are closed too)

rows.name: hybrid invoice, both payee keys
rows.pack_today: nearest: the producer block, scheme hybrid (one classical and one ml-dsa-65 entry)

rows.name: stripping: classical signature removed, PQ key offered alone
rows.pack_today: our reading of §5: a lone ml-dsa-65 entry matches neither scheme, so the block is not ok
rows.pack_with_issuance_member: BadSignature: the PQ signature is bound to the pair

rows.name: stripping: classical signature removed, both keys expected
rows.pack_today: the opposite strip in the producer block: drop the ml-dsa-65 entry and relabel scheme classical-only. This reads valid: true with no policy, and also with both producer keys pinned (producer_signature verified), --trust-set-complete and --require-producer. The same holds when the content is changed and the block re-signed with the classical key alone. It shows only as pq_protected: false and scheme: classical-only. Refused under --require-pq, or when the pinned set holds the ml-dsa-65 key alone. Control: leaving scheme hybrid after the strip reads contradicted. To be fixed in 1.11.0 (a pinned ml-dsa-65 key will require an ml-dsa-65 signature)
rows.pack_with_issuance_member: MissingSignature: the required key set is in the signed data, not a relabelable field
rows.run: run 1.10.0: corrected from the first reading

rows.aer1_anchor: verified (assuming the anchor itself checked; the vector supplies its time)

rows.pack_today: require_pq is a test on the producer block only. A classical-only mandate inside a pack with a pinned hybrid producer block and --require-pq reads require_pq met, valid: true
rows.pack_with_issuance_member: as above, on the enforcer's block time
rows.aer1_anchor: n/a: block time is the enforcer's record, not an anchor

rows.aer1_anchor: absent (a verifier's clock is not an anchor)

rows.pack_today: time_anchor not_evaluated / not_present. require_anchor is unmet only when --require-anchor is given and no anchor is counted
rows.pack_with_issuance_member: policy refused: no trusted time for the transition check (pqam UntrustedTime)

rows.name: ML-DSA-44 only, after the date: refused
rows.pack_today: require_pq is a test on the producer block only. A classical-only mandate inside a pack with a pinned hybrid producer block and --require-pq reads require_pq met, valid: true (and ML-DSA-44 is not in the pack's algorithm set)
rows.aer1_anchor: verified (assuming the anchor itself checked; the vector supplies its time)
